quests.hint: A wedding planner announces: 'Due to the storm warning, the outdoor ceremony will now take place next month instead.'
quests.explanation: POST- means 'after.' POST- + PONE ('put') = POSTPONE, to put off an event until a later time.
quests.instruction: Which prefix fits the meaning below?

quests.hint: Historians describe the economic boom that swept through the country during the years right after the fighting ended.
quests.explanation: POSTWAR is POST- + WAR, relating to the period after a war has ended.
quests.instruction: Which word matches this situation?

quests.hint: After finishing her bachelor's degree, a student enrolls in a two-year master's program to specialize further.
quests.explanation: POST- + GRADUATE = POSTGRADUATE, relating to study that comes after earning an undergraduate degree. PRE- would instead mean before graduating, the opposite stage entirely.
quests.instruction: Which prefix correctly completes this word?

quests.hint: A basketball team plays a handful of practice games in October, before the regular season officially begins in November.
quests.explanation: PRE- + SEASON = PRESEASON, the period before the official season starts. POST- would instead describe games played after the season ends, like playoffs.
quests.instruction: PRE- means 'before.' POST- means 'after.' Which fits here?

quests.hint: After the regular 82-game schedule ends, the top teams compete in a playoff bracket to determine the champion.
quests.explanation: POSTSEASON is POST- + SEASON, the playoff period that comes after the regular season ends — the direct opposite of PRESEASON.
quests.instruction: Which word matches this situation?

quests.hint: An expectant mother attends monthly checkups to monitor the baby's development before it's born.
quests.explanation: PRE- + NATAL ('birth') = PRENATAL, occurring before birth. POST- would instead describe care given after birth, called POSTNATAL — same root, opposite timing.
quests.instruction: PRE- means 'before.' POST- means 'after.' Which fits here?

quests.hint: The exact moment one calendar day ends and the next one begins — 12:00 AM.
quests.explanation: MID- means 'middle.' MID- + NIGHT = MIDNIGHT, the middle point of the night.
quests.instruction: Which prefix fits the meaning below?

quests.hint: A professor schedules a major exam at the halfway point of the semester, before the final.
quests.explanation: MIDTERM is MID- + TERM, occurring at the middle of an academic term.
quests.instruction: Which word matches this situation?

quests.hint: A marathon runner passes the 13-mile marker, exactly half of the full 26-mile course.
quests.explanation: MID- + WAY = MIDWAY, at the halfway point of a distance or process. POST- would instead describe the point after the whole thing is finished, not the halfway mark.
quests.instruction: Which prefix correctly completes this word?

quests.hint: A rookie basketball player scores more points, grabs more rebounds, and shoots a better percentage than every veteran on the team this season.
quests.explanation: OUT- means 'to exceed' or 'to do better than.' OUT- + PERFORM = OUTPERFORM, to perform better than someone else.
quests.instruction: Which prefix fits the meaning below?

quests.hint: Despite being the underdog, one boxer stayed standing through all twelve rounds while his exhausted opponent gave up.
quests.explanation: OUTLAST is OUT- + LAST, to continue existing or functioning longer than something or someone else.
quests.instruction: Which word matches this situation?

quests.hint: A pair of sneakers that fit perfectly last year now pinches a growing kid's toes.
quests.explanation: OUT- + GROW = OUTGROW, to grow too big for something, exceeding its size. OVER- would instead suggest growing excessively in a general sense, not specifically becoming too large for a particular object.
quests.instruction: Which prefix correctly completes this word?

quests.hint: Every year at the holiday party, one coworker tries to top last year's decorations with something even more impressive.
quests.explanation: OUT- + DO = OUTDO, to do better than someone else, specifically in comparison to another person. OVER- would instead mean doing too much of something in general, without necessarily comparing to anyone.
quests.meaningBreakdown: OUT (prefix, 'to exceed, compared to another') + DO (root)
quests.instruction: OVER- means 'too much.' OUT- means 'better than another.' Which fits here?

quests.hint: An employee stays at the office until midnight every night for two straight weeks, skipping meals and sleep to finish a project.
quests.explanation: OVERWORK is OVER- + WORK, to work too much, straining yourself, regardless of how others are doing.
quests.instruction: Which word matches this situation?

quests.hint: At the talent show, one singer's performance was so powerful that it made every other act that night look forgettable by comparison.
quests.explanation: OUT- + SHINE = OUTSHINE, to be noticeably better than someone else in a direct comparison. OVER- wouldn't capture the comparative sense here — 'overshine' isn't standard English, since SHINE specifically takes OUT- for this meaning.
quests.instruction: OVER- means 'too much.' OUT- means 'better than another.' Which fits here?

quests.hint: An airport shuttle glides along a single elevated track connecting the terminals, instead of running on two parallel rails like a regular train.
quests.explanation: MONO- means 'one' or 'single.' MONO- + RAIL = MONORAIL, a train that runs on a single rail.
quests.instruction: Which prefix fits the meaning below?

quests.hint: A kid pedals down the sidewalk on two wheels, balancing with the help of handlebars and momentum.
quests.explanation: BICYCLE is BI- ('two') + CYCLE ('wheel'), a vehicle with two wheels.
quests.instruction: Which word matches this situation?

quests.hint: A geometry teacher draws a shape on the board with exactly three straight sides and three corners.
quests.explanation: TRI- + ANGLE = TRIANGLE, a shape with three angles. BI- would instead mean two, which doesn't match a shape with three distinct corners.
quests.instruction: Which prefix correctly completes this word?

quests.hint: A lecturer reads straight from his notes for an hour in the exact same flat pitch, never once raising or lowering his voice.
quests.explanation: MONO- + TONE = MONOTONE, speech or sound that stays on a single, unchanging pitch.
quests.instruction: Which prefix fits the meaning below?

quests.hint: A child raised by a Spanish-speaking mother and an English-speaking father grows up fluently switching between both languages.
quests.explanation: BILINGUAL is BI- ('two') + LINGUAL ('language'), able to speak two languages fluently.
quests.instruction: Which word matches this situation?

quests.hint: A toddler pedals around the driveway on a small, sturdy ride with one wheel in front and two in back.
quests.explanation: TRI- + CYCLE = TRICYCLE, a vehicle with three wheels — one more than a BICYCLE, since TRI- means three rather than two.
quests.instruction: Which prefix correctly completes this word?

quests.hint: A coach shouts: 'Keep moving toward the goal — don't stop, don't turn back!'
quests.explanation: -WARD means 'in the direction of.' FOR- (an old form meaning 'front') + -WARD = FORWARD, moving toward the front.
quests.instruction: Which suffix fits the meaning below?

quests.hint: A dancer takes several careful steps in reverse, away from the audience, without turning around.
quests.explanation: BACKWARD is BACK + -WARD, moving in the direction of the back or the past.
quests.instruction: Which word matches this situation?

quests.hint: After a long business trip, a traveler finally boards the last flight that will take her back to her own house.
quests.explanation: HOME + -WARD = HOMEWARD, heading in the direction of home. -LY wouldn't fit here — 'homely' is a real word, but it means plain or unattractive, an entirely different meaning from 'heading home.'
quests.instruction: Which suffix correctly completes this word?

quests.hint: A tenant writes next month's date on a rent check so the landlord can't cash it until then.
quests.explanation: POST- + DATE = POSTDATE, to mark a document with a future date. PRE- would instead mean dating something earlier than the current date.
quests.instruction: Which prefix fits this situation?

quests.hint: A soccer player who controls the center of the pitch, linking the defense to the attack.
quests.explanation: MIDFIELD is MID- + FIELD, the middle area of a sports field.
quests.instruction: Which word matches this situation?

quests.hint: At the town meeting, supporters of the new park proposal filled two-thirds of the seats, easily outweighing the small group opposed.
quests.explanation: OUT- + NUMBER = OUTNUMBER, to exceed in number or count. OVER- wouldn't fit — 'overnumber' isn't standard English, since NUMBER specifically pairs with OUT- for this comparative sense.
quests.instruction: Which prefix fits this situation?

quests.hint: A man in his mid-forties suddenly buys a motorcycle and takes up guitar lessons, in what people jokingly call a certain kind of crisis.
quests.explanation: MID- + LIFE = MIDLIFE, the middle stage of a person's life. This final review pulls together the timing prefixes from this unit: PRE- (before), POST- (after), and MID- (middle).
quests.instruction: Phase review: which prefix means 'the middle of'?

quests.hint: A tortoise can survive far longer than nearly every other animal, sometimes outlasting the humans who raised it from a hatchling.
quests.explanation: OUT- + LIVE = OUTLIVE, to live longer than someone or something else, in direct comparison. This reviews OUT-'s comparative sense from OUTPERFORM, OUTLAST, and OUTSHINE earlier in the unit.
quests.instruction: Phase review: which prefix means 'to exceed, compared to another'?

quests.hint: A dental office reminder reads: 'Please schedule your next two cleanings — once in the spring and once in the fall.'
quests.explanation: BI- ('two') + ANNUAL ('yearly,' first introduced all the way back in Level 39) = BIANNUAL, occurring twice a year. Combining a number prefix you just learned with a root from very early in this course is exactly the kind of connection this entire 140-level journey has been building toward.
quests.instruction: Phase capstone: which prefix makes this word mean 'twice a year'?
